Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 103° and a low near 75° tonight. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 67. Our top story today is a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game that left the neighborhood shaken. Overnight, a shooting was reported at a Taco Bell in east Bakersfield, and crews knocked down a fire at a vacant house on King Street. Let’s get you caught up on the night and the day ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight when a witness reported seeing someone shot at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast after the witness described the suspect as a white male in his 40s to 50s wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Earlier, around 2:16 a.m., flames were visible inside a vacant single-story house on King Street with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded — one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back — and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries were unknown. Multiple reports of a grass fire drew a large response — engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer and a helicopter — to southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road. Crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries. The suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 93° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 67. Stay cool and hydrated as we head through the day.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that McFarland police are investigating a homicide after a 26-year-old man was shot and killed Saturday afternoon at the Capri Laundromat in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue.** Officers responded to the scene at approximately 3:18 p.m. and found the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds inside the laundromat. Officers immediately provided medical aid and initiated CPR, but the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. Preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects arrived at the Capri Liquors in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue and confronted the victim inside the Capri Laundromat, which is adjacent to the gas pumps. An argument led to one of the suspects producing a firearm and shooting the victim multiple times. The two suspects then fled the area in an unknown vehicle. No suspects have been identified, no arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown. The victim's identity will be released after next of kin have been notified. McFarland Police Department detectives are actively working the scene and gathering investigative information. Police say there is no current threat to the community, but the public is advised to avoid the area until the scene is processed.

**According to 23ABC, a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game left nearby residents shaken, and a 15-year-old suspect was arrested miles away from the scene.** The scene at Independence High School was chaotic as people tried to understand what had happened after gunshots rang out nearby. Erin Foster lives a few houses down from where the suspect was arrested. She said she was in shock when she learned what had happened. "I like our little neighborhood. That's kind of scary. I have, like, goosebumps. That's kind of scary. And he's 15. Oh, my." Foster said. Foster said she was on her way to her fiancé's workplace when she noticed an unusual scene outside her home. "We couldn't get out of the garage. There was, like, a little Hispanic family sitting over here on. I'm sorry, on the side of the garage, but there were a cop car in these undercover cars, and I was like, 'We can't get out.' So we had to ask him to move, but it was just odd 'cause then they were still here when I came back." Foster said. She said the family remained outside for an extended period of time. "Just odd that there was, like, a little Hispanic family, like a little baby, and like a mom it looked like, and some two, like, toddler little girls, and it was just like, 'Why are they sitting on the side of my garage?'" Foster said. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Eric Celedon said Friday night football games are safe and acknowledged why some community members may be hesitant to attend future games. "So we understand why someone would be fearful to come out, but we want to really reiterate.

**KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** In her statement, Mayor Goh expressed her condolences to the victim’s family and the entire community affected by the tragedy. She emphasized that the safety of our students and community members is of utmost importance and that the city is working closely with law enforcement to ensure justice is served. Mayor Goh urged anyone with information about the incident to come forward and cooperate with the ongoing investigation. Her statement comes as the community grapples with the aftermath of the shooting, which has raised concerns about safety at public events and schools.

## Something good

A local family is hosting a Saturday flea market to raise $8,900 for Villafana’s prosthetic leg. The event aims to support Villafana in obtaining a prosthetic leg, and the community is coming together to help make it happen. It’s a heartwarming reminder of the kindness and generosity that exists right here in Kern County.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several events and meetings on the calendar. On Tuesday, August 26, a Special City Council Meeting is set for 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. On the entertainment front, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio will perform at the Fox Theater today, August 22. The Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 goes on sale at the Fox Theater on August 24. Rodney Carrington takes the stage at the Fox Theater on August 27, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28. Willie Barcena performs at the Fox Theater on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix also takes place at the Fox Theater on August 29. Be sure to check the details and plan accordingly for these events.
